sources.title: Claude Code Action README.md
sources.finding: GitHub Action runs Claude Code on the selected GitHub runner, processes PRs/issues, updates tracking comments and exposes structured outputs.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/setup.md
sources.finding: Repository admins install the app/workflow and set provider secrets; Claude Pro/Max users can generate a Claude Code OAuth token with claude setup-token.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/usage.md
sources.finding: Inputs configure prompt, Claude CLI arguments, OAuth/API credentials, tool restrictions, progress tracking and validated JSON outputs.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/configuration.md
sources.finding: Custom MCP configuration extends built-in GitHub servers. CI workflow and job logs need actions:read on both the token and action configuration.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/security.md
sources.locator: Access control; PR creation; Output security
sources.finding: Write-access checks gate supported actor-driven events, with explicit opt-in exceptions. Default mentions push a branch and return a prefilled PR link. Full debug output can expose private data.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/faq.md
sources.finding: Default workflow creates/pushes commits but directs humans to create PRs and rebase. Destructive Git restrictions are described as system-prompt rules, not a tool-enforced security boundary.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/cloud-providers.md
sources.finding: API execution supports Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry; hosted model access is distinct from the GitHub runner.

sources.title: Claude Code Action docs/custom-automations.md
sources.locator: Mode detection; GitHub events; automated reviews
sources.finding: Explicit prompts enable event-driven automation without mentions; tracking comments are optional. Examples cover PR review and repository updates.

sources.title: Claude Code Action LICENSE
sources.finding: The action repository is MIT licensed.

sources.title: Claude Code Action v1.0.269
sources.finding: Public release v1.0.269 was published 2026-11-06.

sources.title: claude-code-action setup guide
sources.finding: Credentials are an Anthropic API key or an OAuth token that Claude Pro and Max subscribers can generate.

sources.title: Claude Code Action README: Quickstart and License
sources.finding: Setup installs the GitHub app and secrets from Claude Code with /install-github-app or manually; the README names provider credentials but no price or paid plan for the action, and states the MIT licence.

sources.title: Claude Code Action pinned source
sources.finding: The distribution is a composite GitHub Action that installs and runs Claude on the job runner. The repository contains action entrypoints, base-action code, GitHub MCP tools and docs, with no desktop/native-phone application or separately distributed user CLI.

sources.title: Claude Code Action pinned source
sources.finding: The action installs Claude Code and invokes the Claude SDK run path. Its documented executable override expects a Claude Code executable; MCP tool customization does not replace the coding harness.

sources.title: Claude Code Action pinned source
sources.finding: Each workflow invocation prepares one Claude run and writes results to job-scoped RUNNER_TEMP. It reads GitHub issue/PR context, with no native issue database or live multi-human input channel. Separate workflow jobs have no action-wide concurrency lock.

sources.title: Claude Code Action per-user write authorization
sources.finding: Each triggering GitHub actor is checked against repository write/admin access (or an explicitly configured user allowlist). Distinct authorized GitHub users can invoke the action on a shared PR.

sources.title: Claude Code Action shared PR context
sources.finding: Each mention job reads the shared PR body, comments, reviews and changed files. The current trigger comment supplies instructions; previous comments remain context. Multiple authorized people can give successive instructions on the same PR work, with each instruction starting a fresh job and no live input to an already-running job.

sources.title: Claude Code Action shared PR branch
sources.finding: The action checks out the existing PR head branch, so follow-up jobs from distinct GitHub users operate on the same PR work rather than separate private copies.
